# Reviewed database functional roles

1655/1656 eligible objects have bounded role reviews (99.94%). 1 remain unreviewed. A role review is not a complete routine semantic contract, deployment proof or operational acceptance.

Domain and role are separate; multiple roles may apply. The [complete object review ledger](mappings/object-review-ledger.json) explicitly retains every eligible object and unreviewed state. The [curated role records](mappings/functional-roles.json) bind the evidence below.

## Role definitions

- `transactional_state`: Stores mutable business-operation quantities, statuses or execution bookkeeping.
- `configuration`: Stores parameters, definitions or rules that can govern behavior; values and activation were not inspected.
- `master_reference`: Stores reusable identities and descriptive attributes referenced across operations.
- `execution_worklist`: Represents warehouse instruction ordering, assignment and execution state; not the generic vendor process queue.
- `reporting_read_model`: Projects or aggregates stored data for reading; does not imply materialization or measured workload.
- `presentation_metadata`: Stores screen/control definitions, binding properties and display settings.
- `presentation_adapter`: Builds result shapes or selections consumed by a user interface or print-selection flow.
- `orchestration`: Coordinates conditional database calls or multiple implementation steps; caller transactions remain separate.
- `transactional_mutation`: Contains explicit persistent INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE behavior affecting operational state.
- `integration_staging`: Stores interface-shaped payloads and processing indicators; direction, transport and delivery need additional evidence.
- `audit_history`: Stores events, changes or errors; completeness, retention and immutability are not established.
- `workflow_selection`: Builds selection logic for executable warehouse work; not necessarily read-only.
- `utility_transform`: Transforms input into derived values or structured parameters.
- `event_handler`: Defines trigger behavior for a declared DML event; actual execution was not tested.
- `compatibility_declaration`: Retains a procedure signature with no executable body in the captured source; no caller compatibility or invocation is established.
- `paired_structural_record`: Has columns compared with a separately identified record shape; pairing does not establish a copy, archive or retention process.
- `structural_copy`: Has a matching captured column shape; the label does not establish copying provenance, timing, contents or use.
- `activity_measurement`: Provides fields for activity quantities, intervals or costs; formulas, units and actual measured events require separate evidence.
- `request_record`: Provides an identified request record and associated fields; processing, payload grammar and retry behavior remain unestablished.
- `authorization_metadata`: Represents access associations or permission metadata; actual authorization enforcement is not established by the schema.
- `annotation_data`: Stores comments or annotations associated with identifiers; generic identifiers do not establish validated business-object relationships.
- `configuration_payload`: Represents configuration-shaped values; their effective use, precedence and execution are not established.
- `staging_payload`: Provides an intermediate payload shape; a conversion, import or production-consumer lifecycle requires separate evidence.
- `master_data`: Provides reusable entity identities and descriptive fields; current authority, inheritance and consumer behavior require separate evidence.
- `document_metadata`: Stores document references or related status fields; document existence, accessibility and upload completion are not established.
- `payload_shape`: Provides a structurally described payload without sufficient evidence of a producer, consumer or authoritative operational role.
- `retained_record_shape`: Provides a record shape with historical or deleted-state associations; names and fields do not prove events, retention completeness or recoverability.
- `message_payload`: Provides message content and related status fields; transmission, acknowledgment, retry and delivery guarantees are not established.
- `request_state`: Stores request identity, status or timestamps; stored values do not establish processor behavior or physical outcomes.
- `activity_history`: Provides activity record fields; completeness, chronology, duration calculations and actual completed work remain unestablished.
- `content_storage`: Stores text or content segments; reconstruction, ordering, encoding and completeness require caller evidence.
- `configuration_state`: Provides state used to represent settings or counters; effective values, atomic changes and validation require separate evidence.
- `version_metadata`: Stores version or patch provenance fields; this does not establish the installed version of every component.
- `measurement_storage`: Provides instrumentation measurement fields; observed values, instrumentation boundaries and whole-process timing are not established.
- `authorization_payload_shape`: Provides an authorization-shaped payload without established active use or enforcement.
- `integrity_metadata`: Stores hash or integrity-related fields; algorithms, trusted provenance and verification enforcement require separate evidence.
- `metadata_workspace_shape`: Provides a metadata-oriented record shape; temporary names do not establish session scope, consumers or cleanup behavior.
- `association_payload_shape`: Provides identifiers that can represent associations; valid relationships and operational effects require separate evidence.
- `interface_payload`: Provides interface-oriented fields; transport direction, processing, delivery and acknowledgment remain separate claims.
- `activity_state`: Stores activity-related state such as timestamps; current presence, authentication and attendance are not established.
- `identity_metadata`: Stores user or identity-related attributes; authentication mechanisms and effective privileges require separate evidence.

## dbo.ArchivePurgeRunbook

Perform a maintenance runbook that rewrites archive/filter/scheduled-job configuration and can immediately truncate or delete retained history tables. It is a mutating operational routine, not a read-only archive report.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Initialize fixed preference/type groups and a four-entry nonproduction server-name list; choose environment branches using @@SERVERNAME. Initialize history-day constants 7, 30, 90, 180 and 372, delete-loop limit 10 and per-delete TOP limit 500000. These are implementation values, not recommended retention policy. Reclassify selected system-created archive and generic configuration records using process-stamp checks and exclusion lists. Capture a custom-preference exclusion set, normalize USER_DEF fields with environment-specific override handling, and replace selected archive process identifiers. Remove two specifically selected archive preferences and associated filter records. Allocate a system-config numeric key beginning at 5000 using an observed gap or maximum-plus-one fallback, then insert a fixed runbook-related system setting or update the existing setting key. cFilterDelete removes filters and preferences for eligible discovered tables/type records when the applicable environment override is absent. Later updates derive USER_DEF5/ACTIVE/RUN_BY_DEFAULT, USER_DEF6/SAVE_DATA and USER_DEF7/DAYS_HIST with special type groups, exclusions and environment branches. cArchiveCreate enumerates eligible base tables plus synthesized process/transaction history type names and inserts missing archive preferences. Four explicitly added tables are LABEL_PRINT_REQUEST, SSRS_PRINTING_REQUEST, UPLOAD_LOCATION_INVENTORY_ATTRIBUTES and UPLOAD_SERIAL_NUMBER. Parent archive identifiers and dynamic handler identifiers are stored as metadata; those handlers are not invoked by this body. cFilterCreate deletes and rebuilds filter header/detail/statement rows for selected preferences. It stores dynamic filter SELECT text for WORK_ORDER_HEADER and WORK_INSTRUCTION condition tests, LAUNCH_STATISTICS closed tests, and PROCESS_HISTORY/TRANSACTION_HISTORY type tests. It then attaches DATA_FILTER. These filter texts are persisted here rather than executed here. When DeleteLoopLimit is positive, cArchiveTruncate selects child archive tables whose parent preference has saving disabled, active enabled and default-run enabled, plus special process/transaction archive cases when no corresponding type preference requests saving. A metadata row-count existence test narrows targets; each non-null target is immediately TRUNCATE TABLE through QUOTENAME. There is no row/batch cap on a selected truncate. cArchiveDelete selects eligible archive preferences with saving disabled and active/default-run enabled. For each non-null target and positive DAYS_HIST, it constructs an age-based delete: DATE_TIME_STAMP <= CONVERT(DATE, GETUTCDATE()-DAYS_HIST), TOP 500000 ordered by DATE_TIME_STAMP, repeated ten times after one initial existence test. Two subsequent cHistDelete passes target AR_PROCESS_HISTORY and AR_TRANSACTION_HISTORY by configured type with saving disabled and active/default-run enabled. These type-specific deletes have no age predicate and no ORDER BY; they perform TOP 500000 up to ten iterations per cursor row. The same underlying table can be visited through more than one preference. Finally update scheduled-job activation/next-run metadata differently for the fixed environment groups, clear selected PARAMETER_DATA, and adjust active interval jobs with frequency below five minutes by adding five minutes to NEXT_RUN_DATE_TIME and setting minimum frequency five, subject to the stated USER_DEF6 exclusion. No scheduler is invoked here. UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE ARCHIVE_PREFERENCES; UPDATE GENERIC_CONFIG_DETAIL; INSERT/UPDATE SYSTEM_CONFIG_DETAIL. DELETE/INSERT FILTER_CONFIG_HEADER, FILTER_CONFIG_DETAIL and FILTER_STATEMENT; UPDATE SCHEDULED_JOBS. Dynamic TRUNCATE TABLE on selected archive table names; dynamic DELETE CTE on age-qualified selected tables and type-qualified AR_PROCESS_HISTORY/AR_TRANSACTION_HISTORY. Local table-variable inserts and cursor state only in addition to the above persistent effects. sp_executesql for each eligible truncate, age-delete, process-history delete and transaction-history delete. No other stored-procedure call is present. Reading DYNAMIC_CALLING_DETAIL and storing ARCHIVE_PROCESS does not execute that handler. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.AzureSQLMaintenance

Queue and execute index/statistics maintenance with optional persistent logging.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Privately verified operations index/statistics/all and modes smart/dummy; invalid non-NULL mode resets smart, NULL mode remainsNULL. Invalid/NULL operation prints help but does not return: it can still create AzureSQLMaintenanceLog even LogToTable=0, and optional logging/retention still runs. Index discovery uses LIMITED physical stats and index types1/2; smart queues page_count>40 and fragmentation>=5, reorganizing strictly>5 and<30, so exactly5 rebuilds. Dummy means broad real maintenance, not dry-run; OR dummy bypasses preceding queue predicates. Partition rows can produce repeated whole-index commands because partition_number is not inserted into command. Online-support heuristic checks index_id>=1000 only within prefiltered temp data. Statistics selects non-sys rows with modifications or dummy and forms rows/modification info, which can divide by zero. Unordered DELETE TOP1 queue executes each command inside TRY/CATCH, optionally logs command/status using SCOPE_IDENTITY, then continues after errors. Keeps three most recent distinct operation times when logging. Unsuffixed payload uses plain REORGANIZE, REBUILD MAXDOP=1 with ONLINE ON/OFF choice, and UPDATE STATISTICS WITH FULLSCAN. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.dba_UpdateColumn

Add or alter a table column, adjust defaults/checks and propagate to related table variants.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- orchestration: Private fragment inspection confirms dynamic ALTER TABLE. COLUMNPROPERTY IsComputed NULL is treated as absent column and selects ADD with optional default/identity; existing column selects ALTER COLUMN, suppresses those clauses and drops detected default first. Nullable flagY uses NULL, elseNOT NULL. Check-constraint modeY forces nullable column, then if fixed constructed constraint name absent adds WITH NOCHECK CHECK(column IS NOT NULL). In normal modeN an existing dropped default is re-added using caller value or DEFAULT NULL; existing column without prior default does not gain one through this path. Recursively applies to existing AR_/IA_ prefixed tables and special RECEIPT_CONTAINER -> DELETED_RECEIPT_CONTAINER; special recursion omits check-mode argument and uses defaultN. Finally check-modeY with non-NULL default performs unfiltered UPDATE table SET column=default, overwriting existing values. Unquoted names/type/default syntax concatenated into nvarchar500 statement; no allowlist or recursion limit. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.HIST_LogShipDeAlloc

Append inferred before/after transaction history for shipment deallocation.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Builds grouped inventory/allocation-request rows selected by nonzero wave OR nonzero shipment ID, so supplying both widens scope. Fixed direction branch matches destination warehouse/location/attribute ID; other direction matches source scope plus null-safe logistics unit and positive allocated quantity. Both match item, null-safe company/lot. Groups allocation quantities with shipment ID and inventory balances. Identity-order loop accumulates deductions only across consecutive equal warehouse/location/item/lot/logistics-unit/attribute tuples; INSERT has no ORDER BY and tuple omits company, so inferred running balances depend on insertion order and may cross company boundaries. One direction adjusts in-transit, otherwise allocated balances in the table variable. Inserts transaction type200 with ALLOCSUM quantity, before/after inferred balances and second-precision UTC timestamps; after expiration/status retained only if summed balances>0. It does not change LOCATION_INVENTORY or allocation requests. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.HIST_SaveTransHist

Conditionally append transaction history and serial/catch-weight/location attributes, with post-insert validation.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Reads GENERIC_CONFIG_DETAIL by fixed record type/transaction type; preserves non-NULL caller activation but always attempts upload flag lookup. Reads work zone by location+warehouse and normalizes NULL internal-container number to0. Two enabled activation values permit a wide TRANSACTION_HISTORY insert with caller before/after quantities, references and second-rounded UTC times; upload batch is NULL for two config values, fixed sentinel otherwise. Captures @@IDENTITY, which can be affected by trigger identity inserts, rather than SCOPE_IDENTITY. For positive identity adds feature-gated non-NULL catch weight/UM attributes, then serial-argument attributes. If serial attributes were inserted, counts DISTINCT serial GROUP_ID and may raise18 when nonzero count differs from quantity for a fixed transaction type with unchanged suspense quantity. If none inserted, a fixed location-class/transaction-type/changed-onhand branch looks up item tracking (specific OR generic company can yield multiple scalar rows); tracking7 requires a parseable reference with cycle-count requests or raises18. Finally adds nonzero location-attribute ID, but checks stale @error instead of capturing that final INSERT error. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.LBL_GS1AILabelDetail

Prepare bounded GS1 application-identifier detail fields for a shipping container.

Domains: reporting, labels.

- reporting_read_model: First try exactly one requested container with non-NULL container ID/item, setting quantity to1 and unit to CONTAINER_TYPE. Otherwise cursor-group item/company/lot over the requested container and up to three descendant levels, summing each group; compare successive groups for differing item/company or lot and retain coded errors in variables. This is bounded nesting, not arbitrary recursion. Resolve sequence1 unit with ITMfn_RtrvUnitOfMeasure, then grouped GTIN item metadata and item cross-reference; duplicate cross-reference rows produce a coded fallback. Read lot expiry and UNION ALL active/retained serial rows for the same bounded container tree; more than one serial row produces a coded fallback. Apply one opaque expiry sentinel and emit fields; AI_QTY depends on cross-reference first character and AI_EXP on NULL expiry. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.Load_Generic_Config_Dtl

Insert selected staged generic configuration rows into live configuration.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Cursor selects record type, non-error user stamp and nonprocessed flag, ordered SYS1VALUE descending; NULL flags are excluded by <>. ## dbo.LoadAdditionalConfigsSummary

Build a selected configuration-count summary from a JSON selection document. The retained body constructs dynamic UNION SELECT statements over a fixed set of configuration tables; it does not load or change those configuration rows.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- reporting_read_model: Trim @configsToLoad, parse top-level properties with OPENJSON and CROSS APPLY OPENJSON to their values, aggregate single-quote QUOTENAME values into a parenthesized comma-separated list, and store key/value strings in #configsKeyValData. Empty-array properties receive a separate empty-string row. The generic, system and filter header/detail branches inject these quoted value lists into fixed RECORD_TYPE IN predicates. Generic and filter summaries count non-null detail columns through LEFT JOIN and group by the header record type. The system-config branch adds a fixed exclusion combining a small SYS_KEY list and RECORD_TYPE. Because the extra predicate references the nullable detail side, a header with no matching detail is filtered by three-valued logic rather than reliably returned as a zero-count header. Other branches are selected by property existence plus nonempty serialized value checks; some additionally use LIKE against the serialized value. They then append fixed aggregate SELECT templates, often counting an entire table rather than applying each selected element as a row predicate. The generated query begins with a leading UNION token; a final prefix check removes six characters before sp_executesql. The temporary table is dropped at the normal tail. There is no local error cleanup path. Creates, inserts into and drops local #configsKeyValData. No persistent DML appears in the retained body or reviewed dynamic SELECT templates. sp_executesql @query without a separate parameter definition/value list; constructed input is used in fixed IN-list branches. No other procedure call is present. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.MOVECLS_MineMovementClassAnalysisData

Replace movement-class analysis for a warehouse using transaction activity and zero-hit inventory.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Window ends at tomorrow UTC midnight and starts @Days earlier (default90), including the current partial day. Deletes existing analysis for warehouse first. Aggregates fixed direction and transaction types40,60,100,130,120,240,250,360 from current history plus optional archive when flag=Y, grouped item/company/location/UM/class. UNION, not UNION ALL, can collapse equal current/archive aggregate rows. Item join accepts matching company OR either sideNULL, allowing fanout. Permanent=Y additionally joins current inventory by location/warehouse/lot/company without item/logistics-unit/attribute match and requires PERMANENT<>N, allowing multiplication across inventory rows. Otherwise no permanent restriction. Adds positive-onhand inventory with zero hits where no existing analysis item/company/location match; totals then represent onhand for zero-hit rows versus movement quantity for hit rows. Dates/days/status configuration and input flags are not validated. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.PMN_Trace

Control three SQL trace streams and report their status, with variant-specific dispatch.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Reads configured IDs/file names/max sizes for long-running, blocked and deadlock traces. Condition0 stops active positive IDs, closes them and sets configured IDs0. Condition1 creates IDs<1, configures the explicit event/column matrix (long IDs10,43,45,12,41; blocked137; deadlock148), applies active TRACE_FILTER rows to long trace, starts streams and stores IDs. Creation return code is assigned but not checked. @filterValue declared nvarchar without length is one character, truncating string filter values; default bigint2000000 is overwritten by cursor values and no filter is applied if cursor empty. @LongTraceID initialized twice while deadlock ID remainsNULL until lookup, so missing config can skip creation then passNULL to calls. Default condition2 skips control but still reads status/path; output path truncated to80 characters. PMN_Trace first tests @@version against a fixed pattern. Matching branch calls PMN_EVENT_SESSION with condition plus startDateTime, while captured child signature accepts only condition: static argument-count mismatch. Other branch uses captured underscore column names and appends the caller startDateTime string directly to filenames; startDateTime has no default. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.RPT_MasterBOLConsolHeader

Return consolidated master bill-of-lading header and a separate container detail result set.

Domains: reporting, labels.

- reporting_read_model: Set @company=MIN(company) only when COUNT(DISTINCT company)=1 for load shipments. Header load inner warehouse then left company/address/carrier generic-service joins; ship-from address precedence is warehouse-company then company then warehouse by row presence. Ship-to comes from SHIPPING_ADDRESS at load and opaque record_type. Underlying-BOL helper supplies bol_list. Second SELECT takes ALL containers for load shipments, left shipment detail and NMFC config by record_type/identifier; order_num customer_po else ERP order; nonNULL hazardous_code emits opaque marker. Neither result has ORDER BY. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.RTH_UpdateHeader

Refresh receipt header status from open detail quantity and container statuses, then queue close alerts.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Resolves configured closed status and header warehouse. Positive SUM open quantity forces the configured action status as trailing; otherwise MIN container status. Leading is MAX container status; NULL new values preserve old status. On inequality changes, stores warehouse-local date without time and clears failure flag. CLOSE_DATE is set to UTC only when trailing changes to closed; it is not cleared when reopened and a NULL old status makes <> unknown. Always updates process/UTC stamp. Then inserts matching active close-alert requests if no alert/source/identifier match exists; no warehouse restriction on alert definition and NOLOCK NOT EXISTS is not concurrency-safe. Already-closed headers can trigger absent requests even without a current transition. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.SDB_MoveQtyToSts

Move a quantity between the ten status buckets of a shipment detail.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Reads all10 status/quantity pairs and shipment number with UPDLOCK. Helpers locate source status and quantity; subtracts requested move quantity. Missing source position<=0 or negative remainder errors. Positive remainder updates source bucket; otherwise shifts later pairs left and clears final slot. Locates destination after this removal, adds move amount to existing quantity or finds sorted insertion position and shifts pairs right before inserting. No guard for an eleventh occupied status: inserting while10 remain can overwrite/discard a final pair. Negative move quantity is not rejected and can reverse quantities; NULL arithmetic can bypass guards and follow removal branch. ## dbo.SDB_MoveQtyToSts01

Move a quantity between the ten status buckets of a shipment detail.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Reads all10 status/quantity pairs and shipment number with UPDLOCK. Helpers locate source status and quantity; subtracts requested move quantity. Missing source position<=0 or negative remainder errors. Positive remainder updates source bucket; otherwise shifts later pairs left and clears final slot. Locates destination after this removal, adds move amount to existing quantity or finds sorted insertion position and shifts pairs right before inserting. No guard for an eleventh occupied status: inserting while10 remain can overwrite/discard a final pair. Negative move quantity is not rejected and can reverse quantities; NULL arithmetic can bypass guards and follow removal branch. Writes all10 pairs plus process/UTC stamp by line ID, leaving TOTAL_QTY unchanged. The 01 variant stops after writing and checking the detail UPDATE; it does not refresh the shipment header despite calculating old leading/trailing values. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.sp_generate_insert_script

Generate INSERT script text by dynamically reading rows from catalog-selected tables.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- orchestration: NULL table-name mask becomes wildcard. Selects sysobjects typesU andS without schema and iterates names in lexical order. Uses old syscolumns type/status metadata, excludes type37, stores column names in nvarchar30 and builds nvarchar4000 left/right query strings. Character type39/47 branch escapes single quotes; type35 text is converted to nvarchar1000; datetime types58/61/111 to nvarchar20; other types to nvarchar99. Generated query reads full table with no row filter and orders by generated first expression. Schema/name quoting, wide rows, long columns, types and NULL conversions can yield incomplete or invalid script text. It does not validate generated script roundtrip or execute INSERT/IDENTITY commands. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.STH_UpdateHeader

Roll shipment detail/root-container status into the header and linked load.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Unbounded loop condition rowsUpdated=0. Usually derives minimum detail status1 and maximum helper-leading status, subject to a container-existence branch, then extends range with root containers (PARENT NULL). Highest per-line quantity at997 can override minimum via configured action status, capped by maximum. Invalid/nonpositive/NULL statuses and minimum>=994 invoke configured defaults selected by old leading>=300 or minimum997. Change flag is sticky across retries. On change, inserts active forward-progress alert requests before header update with NOLOCK NOT EXISTS; SCOPE_IDENTITY captures only one ID even if multiple alerts insert, so retry correction changes only that row. Header compares both old statuses, then updates both status dates to warehouse-local date, resets failure flags and stamps UTC. NULL old status or concurrent changes can prevent match indefinitely. On changed completion, refreshes positive linked load. No bounded retry/atomic transaction. Evidence: E1.

E1: [DB Architecture/sql/2065754762.sql](sql/2065754762.sql), lines 1-224; SHA-256 `363c6a189e422cd4fa34382a8cedee3a7e543130d41a857d6a91d687e72a4bf0`. ## dbo.STH_UpdateLoad

Roll linked shipment status range into a shipping-load header.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Unbounded optimistic loop reads MIN shipment trailing/MAX leading and old load statuses with NOLOCK. Default condition tests minimum<=0 twice, omitting a maximum<=0 test; after correcting minimum, maximum fallback again checks minimum, so nonpositive maximum may remain. Sticky StatusChanged flag compares old/new using <>. On change updates both statuses, both warehouse-local date-only status dates, failure flags and stamps, guarded by equality to both old values. NULL old values can suppress change or prevent update when the other status changes; concurrent mutation has no retry limit. No shipment/order update is called. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.trace_ILS

Control three SQL trace streams and report their status, with variant-specific dispatch.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Reads configured IDs/file names/max sizes for long-running, blocked and deadlock traces. Condition0 stops active positive IDs, closes them and sets configured IDs0. Condition1 creates IDs<1, configures the explicit event/column matrix (long IDs10,43,45,12,41; blocked137; deadlock148), applies active TRACE_FILTER rows to long trace, starts streams and stores IDs. Creation return code is assigned but not checked. @filterValue declared nvarchar without length is one character, truncating string filter values; default bigint2000000 is overwritten by cursor values and no filter is applied if cursor empty. @LongTraceID initialized twice while deadlock ID remainsNULL until lookup, so missing config can skip creation then passNULL to calls. Default condition2 skips control but still reads status/path; output path truncated to80 characters. Legacy trace_ILS reads traceid/columnid/minValue/filterValue/logicalOp/comparisonOp identifiers, whereas captured TRACE_INFO/TRACE_FILTER schema has TRACE_ID/COLUMN_ID/MIN_VALUE/FILTER_VALUE/LOGICAL_OP/COMPARISON_OP; underscore differences are a static binding concern. File suffix derives from locally formatted GETDATE. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.TRAV_EX08_ScheduledJob

Escalate lane work and maintain pallet/destination assignments through several independent steps.

## dbo.ValidateSerialNumberIsUnique

Check serial uniqueness under global and item-scoped duplicate rules.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- reporting_read_model: Privately verified configuration flag Y selects item-scoped checks; otherwise checks all SERIAL_NUMBER rows. Item/company context precedence is nonzero receipt container, then location inventory, then shipping container. Under global Y plus @allowDuplicates=N, checks each attachment type for same item, null-safe company and ISNULL(template,0) equality. Other @allowDuplicates values use item only, without company/template filtering. Every check excludes OBJECT_ID=@objectId using <>: default NULL objectId makes this predicate unknown and can report1 even for duplicate serials. Default NULL serial also cannot match. Config scalar subquery can fail on duplicate rows; no warehouse restriction or uniqueness-enforcing write. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.WAP_ValInboundReq

Delete an inbound alert request when its receipt context or configured criteria fail.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Loads receipt fields by internal receipt number. NULL trailing status, including missing receipt, immediately deletes request by request ID and returns. Otherwise iterates criteria joined to operator metadata by name and alert type, for alert ID. Maps identifier/carrier/company/priority/receipt type/ship-from/source/line/value/weight fields into nvarchar50, then compares UPPER strings even for numeric data. Privately verified operator mapping rejects the inverse of each requested comparison; unrecognized operator falls back to equality. First failure ends loop and deletes request. ## dbo.WAP_ValOutboundReq

Delete an outbound alert request when its shipment context or configured criteria fail.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- transactional_mutation: Loads shipment-header-view values by internal shipment number; NULL trailing status deletes request immediately. Iterates alert criteria joined by name/type. Maps shipment fields into nvarchar50. Privately verified TOTAL_LINES, TOTAL_VALUE and TOTAL_WEIGHT receive CAST AS numeric comparisons (default zero scale), so fractional precision is not preserved and malformed criteria can error. All other fields, including priority/internal order number, compare UPPER text. Operators use inverse rejection tests; unknown operator defaults to equality. Empty criteria or NULL comparison results can leave the request intact. First failure deletes by request ID without warehouse/context relationship guard. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.wm_RItemUnitOfMeasure07

Compute an insertion sequence from a storage-template unit sequence.

Domains: warehouse, operations.

- reporting_read_model: Compute an insertion sequence from a storage-template unit sequence. Item presence chooses item/company or item-class paths; unordered TOP 1 item template lookups and unordered variable assignment can select ambiguous candidates. A found sequence below one returns -1; otherwise return ISNULL(MAX(existing preceding unit sequence),0)+1. A NULL template sequence takes the ELSE path and returns 1 because the preceding comparison finds no rows. No unit row is inserted. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.WOHB_UpdateQtyAvailToBuild

Domains: work, configuration, reporting.

- presentation_adapter: Parse warehouse plus category/customer/ship-to/work group; translate each unassigned label to NULL and apply all four exact-or-both-NULL filters. Join WORK_INSTRUCTION to SHIPMENT_HEADER by internal shipment number with two coded internal types and nonclosed condition, matching source OR destination warehouse. Distinct work-type/work-unit/internal-shipment tuples feed COUNT(work unit), not COUNT DISTINCT, per type; same work unit in different shipments can count more than once. Order chart DATA descending. Summary computes per-condition distinct work-unit counts, instruction counts and estimated-time sums, then sums those groups; open/in-process totals use coded conditions. Closed instruction count uses WORK_INSTRUCTION_VIEW and DATE_TIME_STAMP>=UTC minus1hour with the same drill filters. Evidence: E1.

## dbo.WTH_UpdateDetailOverPick

Apply overpick quantity and totals to a work detail.

Domains: work, configuration, reporting.

- transactional_mutation: Validate positive detail ID. Direction0 reads source quantity/line into otherwise unused variables, zeroes FROM_QTY, adds requested qty to TO_QTY and changes total QUANTITY by requested-minus-existing source; scale totals/converted qty to that new amount, zeroing them if nonpositive.
